Dispatched by the factory from `dev.task` [`00d468bb-eb36-406c-879b-5d45edc74d3e`](00d468bb-eb36-406c-879b-5d45edc74d3e).

**This PR was written by an agent and checked by the dispatcher.** The dispatcher
runs declared verification in the isolated clone before opening a PR. It
bootstraps a clone-local `venv/` from the repo's Python dependency declarations
and adds `PyYAML` because the committed EA/checker scripts import `yaml` without
owning that dependency in a requirements file. That path is slower than relying
on the host interpreter, but it keeps task specs faithful and makes
`venv/bin/python ...`, `python ...`, and `python3 ...` declarations resolve
inside the clone.

Change kind: behavioral

Applies: PRIN-008, PRIN-011

## Verification checkout

Declared verification below ran against `d5e4c185898df8bcb8a60b6036f7cb4f34b1ce2e` of `main`. The dispatcher refuses to clone (so this PR would not exist) unless both hold at dispatch time: the worker checkout's own revision is a confirmed, current ancestor of local `main` (`worker_revision.ensure_checkout_is_current_with_main`), and `main` itself is a confirmed ancestor-or-equal of its own tracking upstream -- carries no commit absent from it (`dispatch.ensure_base_ref_current`; `BaseRefStatus.wrong`). Date this evidence against that commit, not against when the PR was opened.

## Intent

dev.finding 3dc4a938 (medium, 2026-10-02): apps/factory-dispatcher/dispatch.py's open_pull_request renders the worker's own report as {worker_note.strip()[:4000]} between two ``` lines (the 'Worker's own report' section, around :4076-4080 at main), with no escaping. A worker report that contains its own fenced block closes the dispatcher's fence early, so the rest of the report renders as live PR-body text; .github/workflows/lint.yml's 'Check PR body for change kind' step (fence-aware awk: toggles on any line starting with ```, then counts lines matching ^[[:space:]]*Change kind:[[:space:]]*(structural|behavioral)[[:space:]]*$) then counts a second declaration and fails the PR. Measured: PR 1131 failed this way on 2026-10-02 and PR 1061 on 2026-09-27. Separately, the 4000-character cap cut reports off mid-word on PR 1131 and PR 1149, and the PR body then gave no sign it was truncated; release gates on 8 of 13 first-round verdicts in the week to 2026-10-03 required a PR-body-only change, several because the report was cut off before its acceptance-criterion evidence (release-manager measurement, 2026-10-03). Two readers must both see the report as one inert block: GitHub's CommonMark renderer, for which a fence closes on a line of up to three spaces' indentation followed by a run of at least as many of the same fence character (``` or ~~~), and the CI awk above, which toggles on any line beginning with ``` at column 0 and counts declaration lines even when indented. So indentation alone is not enough (the awk counts an indented declaration), and a longer outer fence is not enough (the awk toggles on any ``` run). This bead makes the report container safe for both and makes truncation visible. The worker persona (docs/agents/polecat-developer.md) is updated by the outer loop in the PR that files this spec, telling workers the report is pasted verbatim, capped, and must lead with acceptance-criterion evidence; docs/** is forbidden here.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-1: ONE INERT CONTAINER. open_pull_request renders the worker's report so that, for ANY worker_note string, (a) the CI awk extracted read-only from .github/workflows/lint.yml's 'Check PR body for change kind' step counts exactly one declaration in the whole body (the dispatcher's own), and (b) no line between the dispatcher's opening and closing container lines matches the CommonMark fence-line pattern ^ {0,3}(`{3,}|~{3,}) unless it is the dispatcher's own closing line. Any transformation of worker lines needed to achieve this is applied to the report text only, is the minimum that achieves it (for example a short visible marker on the offending lines; keep it short, since a report made entirely of fence lines must not push the body past GitHub's 65,536-character limit), and keeps every other report line byte-identical. When, and only when, at least one line was neutralised, a one-line note inside the section says how many lines were neutralised and why; a report with nothing to neutralise gets no note.
- AC-2: THE CASES. A parametrised test drives open_pull_request (through the existing run seam, no network) with worker_note values that either break a reader on main today (the nested ``` block, the three-space-indented fence, the four-backtick fence) or pin a property the container must keep (the rest), and asserts AC-1's (a) and (b) on the rendered body for each, using explicit pytest ids per case: a nested ``` fenced block containing 'Change kind: behavioral'; a bare 'Change kind: structural' line; the same line indented by four spaces; a line '   ```' (three-space indent); a '~~~' fence; a '````' four-backtick fence; a 'Release-gate: MERGE' line (dev.finding 807baee1's reader is separate, but the line must stay inside the container); and a report with no fence at all, which must render byte-identical to today apart from the cap change. The awk is run as a subprocess using the program text extracted from .github/workflows/lint.yml with the standard library only (no PyYAML: CI's Python Unit & Contract Tests job does not declare it); CI runs on the self-hosted host-b runner, where the Validate PR Change Kind step already runs this awk, and the factory runs on macOS, both of which have awk. The test therefore fails if the workflow's parser changes in a way this container no longer satisfies.
- AC-3: THE CAP AND ITS NOTICE. The report cap rises from 4000 to 12000 characters. When the stripped report is longer than the cap, the body states, outside the container and directly after it, '[worker report truncated: <shown> of <total> characters shown]' with the real numbers; when it is not longer, no such line appears. A test covers both, and a test asserts a 12000-character report is shown whole.
- AC-4: NOTHING ELSE MOVES. Every other PR-body section renders exactly as before (the existing open_pull_request body tests in tests/test_dispatch.py pass unchanged, for example test_open_pull_request_body_is_unchanged_when_traceability_absent); no spawn site, argv shape or environment changes (tests/test_spawn_inventory.py and tests/test_spawn_env_fixture.py pass); dispatch.py's net growth is at most +30 lines (report wc -l before and after against the merge base).
- AC-5: MUTATION. Each turns at least one test red: rendering the report with today's plain ``` wrapper and no neutralisation; neutralising only column-0 ``` lines (the three-space and tilde cases must catch it); dropping the truncation notice; keeping the 4000 cap.
- AC-6: STAGE BEFORE THE FINAL RUN, AND REPORT. Run `git add` on every new file before the final verification run. Your final report leads with: the neutralisation rule in one sentence, each AC-2 case with the test node id that covers it, the collected test count before and after against the merge base, wc -l for dispatch.py before and after, and each AC-5 mutation with the test it turns red. Do not put a triple-backtick fence or a line starting 'Change kind:' in your report (this very defect).

## Declared scope

Allowed: apps/factory-dispatcher/dispatch.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/
Forbidden: .github/**, .github/workflows/**, .gitignore, AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, docs/**, infrastructure/**, scripts/**, apps/lifeops-console/**, apps/mcp-hub/**, apps/substrate/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/activities/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/guards.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/containment.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/git_control.py, apps/factory-dispatcher/tasks/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/workflows/**, apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/fixtures/**

Dispatcher scope verdict: **all changes within scope**

## Verification the task asked for

- `cd apps/factory-dispatcher && python -m pytest tests/test_dispatch.py tests/test_spawn_inventory.py tests/test_spawn_env_fixture.py -q`
- `cd apps/factory-dispatcher && python -m pytest tests/ -q`
- `python scripts/check-repo-invariants.py`

## Dispatcher verification

## Environment parity with CI

- **Neutralized:** ambient git config. Declared verification runs with `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` pointed at `/dev/null` and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` set, so `init.defaultBranch` and any committer identity from the operator's `~/.gitconfig`, a conventional `/etc/gitconfig`, *or* a vendor-baked installation-scope config (Apple's git ships one CI has no equivalent of -- PR #792's gate caught that `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` alone doesn't hide it) are invisible to it, matching a CI runner that has none of the three (#765's `create_repo_with_tracking_main` specimen).
- **Reported, not neutralized:** this clone carries a local `main` branch tracking `origin/main`, because the dispatcher's own later git operations in this same clone need one. CI's `actions/checkout` on a PR instead leaves a detached HEAD with no local `main`. A declared command that depends on `main` being a resolvable ref -- not merely on config -- can still pass here and fail in CI (#759).
- **Undetectable by this pre-check:** anything not git-configuration or dependency-presence shaped -- network reachability, OS/platform differences, resource limits, and any ambient environment variable outside `VERIFICATION_ENV_ALLOWLIST` that CI also lacks. A green pre-check establishes parity only for the two points above, not general CI-equivalence.

## Worker's own report

```
Everything checks out. Final report below.

The neutralization rule: any report line matching GitHub's CommonMark fence-line pattern (0-3 spaces, then ≥3 backticks or tildes) gets a backslash inserted right after its indentation and right before the run — this pattern is a superset of what the CI change-kind awk's own `/^```/` toggle reacts to, so defusing it keeps the awk's `in_fence` state true for the dispatcher's entire fenced block, which also shields any embedded `Change kind:` line regardless of its own indentation.

AC-2 cases and their test node ids (all in `apps/factory-dispatcher/tests/test_dispatch.py`):
- nested fence + Change kind → `test_worker_report_container_is_inert_for_both_readers[nested_fenced_block_with_change_kind]`
- bare Change kind line → `[bare_change_kind_line]`
- indented Change kind line → `[change_kind_indented_four_spaces]`
- three-space-indented fence → `[three_space_indented_fence]`
- tilde fence → `[tilde_fence]`
- four-backtick fence → `[four_backtick_fence]`
- Release-gate: MERGE line → `[release_gate_merge_line]` plus `test_worker_report_release_gate_line_stays_inside_the_container`
- no fence at all → `[no_fence_plain_report]` plus `test_worker_report_with_no_fence_renders_byte_identical_to_legacy`

Collected tests: 3089 before → 3104 after (merge base `d5e4c185`). `dispatch.py`: 7202 → 7230 lines (wc -l), net +28 (diff: +33/-5), under the +30 cap.

Mutations and the test each turns red:
- today's plain wrapper, no neutralization → 7 tests fail (all `worker_report_container_is_inert_for_both_readers` fence cases, the note test, both cap tests)
- neutralizing only column-0 ``` (awk's own narrow trigger) → `[three_space_indented_fence]` and `[tilde_fence]` fail
- dropping the truncation notice → `test_worker_report_cap_truncates_and_states_it` fails
- keeping the 4000 cap → `test_worker_report_cap_shows_a_12000_character_report_whole` and `test_worker_report_cap_truncates_and_states_it` fail

Verification run: `cd apps/factory-dispatcher && python -m pytest tests/test_dispatch.py tests/test_spawn_inventory.py tests/test_spawn_env_fixture.py -q` → 365 passed. `python -m pytest tests/ -q` → 3072 passed, 32 skipped (pre-existing skips, unrelated). `python scripts/check-repo-invariants.py` → all invariants passed. All three ran against a venv built fresh in `$TMPDIR` (no system Python had pytest); no repo file reflects that venv.

Residual (per the binding Q&A, not addressed here): readers that ignore fences entirely — `find_bead_id`/`BEAD_LINE_RE`, `OUTER_LOOP_RE`, and `merge-pr.sh`'s provenance grep — can still be steered by a line inside the worker report; this container fix only closes the two readers AC-1 names.
```
